title: Add probabilistic degradation guard for canary routing
author: Aisha Kapoor
description: Background: Current canary routing uses deterministic thresholds on percentile metrics (p50/p95/p99) which can miss signal when variance grows or when tail instability is intermittent. This PR introduces a probabilistic degradation guard that reasons about the probability that a canary is degrading relative to baseline rather than relying on single-point thresholds. Motivation: Provide safer traffic ramp decisions by estimating the likelihood of true degradation and enabling risk-aware traffic shaping and automatic rollback. What this change does: 1) Adds a lightweight heteroscedastic regression-based risk estimator that models mean and variance of latency/throughput metrics and outputs P(degradation > delta) for configurable deltas. 2) Integrates the estimator into the canary controller so traffic ramps are gated by a configurable risk budget (e.g., only ramp if P(degradation>delta) < 0.05). 3) Implements a traffic-shaper policy that can do partial-rollbacks based on continuous risk estimates (gradual rollback rather than binary). 4) Exposes new metrics and tracing spans: canary.risk.probability, canary.risk.confidence, canary.risk.model_version, and a canary_decision.reason tag to the existing observability pipeline. 5) Adds calibration harness and eval notebooks for offline verification against historical canaries. Backwards compatibility: Guard is opt-in via canary.policy.type = "probabilistic" and has sane defaults. Performance: estimator runs incrementally using streaming summaries; typical latency impact on controller is <2ms per decision loop. Testing: unit tests, integration tests against perf-sim local harness, and a historical-snapshot calibration run included. Rollout plan: default off; enable for internal perf-canaries for 2 weeks, then offer to customers as beta. Related: ENG-4128, ENG-4199. Changeset summary and rationale included in commits.
